articles.title: Calm start to the week after a turbulent Friday
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Weak US labor market
 on Friday provided support to the world's stock markets and the S&P closed at +0.7%, despite a slight slowdown on Friday evening. It is mostly up in Asia (Nikkei +2.4%) and stock market futures point to small movements initially.
Not so many international statistics during the week, but minutes from the Fed and the ECB may be able to give some small clues about interest rate policy in the autumn.
 The market has lowered the probability of interest rate hikes in October to very low levels for both the Fed and the ECB and is also starting to hesitate a bit about a hike later this year, although the probability of an interest rate hike at the end of the year is still very high. Signals of both inflation and growth in the near term are mixed, as illustrated by the weak employment development in September (read more 
here
). Expectations of interest rate hikes during the autumn and winter were lowered and the probability of a hike in October is now only 15-20%. In addition to low employment and higher unemployment, wage growth continued to slow to historically low levels. Interesting for the inflation rate, although Fed Governor Warsh for some unclear reason played down the importance of wages for inflation.
The right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro 
(son of Jair Bolsonaro) won the first round of the presidential election in Brazil with 47% of the vote against 45% for incumbent president Lula da Silva (left). The second round will take place on October 25 and according to Polymarket, the probability of Bolsonaro becoming the new president has increased to 83% from about 60%.
The turbulence in the fixed income market continues 
and after a volatile day, European yields closed just over 5 basis points lower. The interest rate margin between France and Germany closed unchanged after increasing by 20 basis points earlier on Friday. However, US yields increased by 10 basis points during the evening.
Nordic key stories
Norway's CPI-ATE is expected to rise by 3.1%,
which is one-tenth higher than in August and two-tenths higher than Norges Bank's forecast. Norges Bank lowered its forecast for the CPI-ATE by half a percent for the next few months. We see upside risks in the short term, although we are a little more optimistic further ahead. Our assessment is that Norges Bank – with a policy rate of 4.50% – has now made a clear hike.    
A lot of Swedish statistics will be published during the week, and the flash estimate for the CPI is of course the most interesting. 
 Our forecast is that the CPIF excluding energy will increase from 0.5% to 0.7% in September, which is in line with consensus and the Riksbank. A weaker krona and indirect effects from energy indicate that inflation will rise gradually, but so far there are no clear signs of higher core inflation in either Swedish or international indicators. Prices for package holidays, hotels and car rentals rose more than usual during the summer and could fall back a little more than usual in September, which is a downside risk to our forecast. On Friday, growth data for August will be published, and strong sentiment indicators point to a clear upward rebound, after slightly weak figures in July. The momentum for growth appears to have strengthened in the third quarter, but high energy prices and higher interest rates suggest that the outlook going forward is not as bright. According to our assessment, CPIF inflation will rise to 1.6% in September, and the combination of high world market prices and the reversal of tax cuts on fuel means that inflation looks set to rise to 2.5% towards the end of the year. It remains to be seen how the ultimately slightly more optimistic households will react to a new cost shock. The Riksbank's interest rate hikes will push up total CPI inflation to 2.5-3% in 2027, which suggests clear downside risks for our optimistic GDP forecast for 2027.
SEB's Housing Price Indicator, which was published this morning, rises by 2 points to 43
. The indicator has been fairly stable in 2026 at relatively high levels and our forecast – that house prices will rise by 5% this year – seems to be on track. Early and larger expected interest rate hikes from the Riksbank are a downside risk for house prices in 2027. Mäklarstatistik presents house prices for August on Thursday. More about our indicator 
here.
Attempts to form a new Swedish government are continuing, 
but the conditions for a red-green government so far look uncertain. The Center Party has invited the Social Democratic Party, the Liberal Party, and the Green Party to a joint situation review on Friday, but at the same time sticks to its red line of not being in the same government as the Left Party. The Center Party, Magdalena Andersson, is to report the results of its soundings to the Speaker by October 12, but can request more time if meaningful talks are still ongoing. The Speaker has said that a vote on the prime minister will be held when the exploratory mission is completed. 
Stora Coop is reducing the prices of 600 of its best-selling products
 by an average of 6.5% nationwide. This is at least another sign that competitive pressure in the grocery trade is high and does not provide any support for any broad new price increase for food right now.

articles.title: Lugn veckostart efter svängig fredag”
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Svag amerikansk arbetsmarknad
 gav i fredags gav stöd till världens börser och S&P stängde på +0,7%, trots en viss avmattning under fredagskvällen. Det är mestadels upp i Asien (Nikkei +2,4%) och börsterminerna pekar på små rörelser inledningsvis.
Inte så mycket internationell statistik under veckan men protokoll från Fed och ECB kanske kan ge lite små ledtrådar om räntepolitiken under hösten.
 Marknaden har dragit ned sannolikheten för räntehöjningar i oktober till mycket låga nivåer för både Fed och ECB och börjar även tveka lite om en höjning senare i år, även om sannolikheten för en räntehöjning för årsskiftet fortfarande är mycket hög. Signalerna om både inflation och tillväxt under närmaste tiden spretar vilket illustreras av den svaga sysselsättningsutvecklingen under september (läs mer 
här
). Förväntningarna på räntehöjningar under hösten och vintern skruvades ned och sannolikheten för en höjning i oktober är nu bara xx%. Förutom låg sysselsättning och högre arbetslöshet fortsatte lönetillväxten att avta till historiskt sett låga nivåer. Intressant för inflationstakten, även om Fed-chefen Warsh av lite oklar anledning spela ned lönernas betydelse för inflationen.
Höger-kandidaten Flavio Bolsonaro (son till Jair Bolsonaro) vann första rundan av president valet i Brasilien med 47% av rösterna mot 45% för sittande presidenten Lula da Silva (vänster). Andra rundan äger rum den 25:e oktober och enligt Polymarket har sannolikheten ökat för att Bolsonaro blir ny president till 83% från ungefär 60%.
Turbulensen på räntemarknaden fortsätter 
och efter en svängig dag stängde de europeiska räntorna drygt 5 räntepunkter lägre. Räntemarginalen mellan Frankrike och Tyskland stängde oförändrad efter att ha ökat med 20 räntepunkter tidigare under fredagen. USA-räntorna vände dock upp med 10 punkter under kvällen.
Norges KPI-JAE förväntas stiga med 3,1%
 vilket är en tiondel högre än i augusti och två tiondelar högre än Norges Banks prognos. Norges Bank sänkte sin prognos för KPI-JAE med en halv procent för de närmaste månaderna. Vi ser uppåtrisker på kort sikt även om vi är lite mer optimistiska längre fram. Vår bedömning är att Norges Bank – med en styrränta på 4,50% – nu har höjt klart.  
Sverige
En hel del statistik publiceras under veckan och snabbestimatet för KPI är naturligtvis mest intressant. 
Vår prognos är att KPIF exkl. energi ökar från 0,5% till 0,7% i september, vilket är i linje med konsensus och Riksbanken. Svagare krona och indirekta effekter från energi talar för att inflationen stiger gradvis men än så länge syns inga tydliga tecken på högre kärninflation i vare sig svenska eller internationella indikatorer. Priserna på paketresor, hotell och biluthyrning steg mer än vanligt under sommaren och skulle kunna falla tillbaka lite mer än vanligt i september, vilket är en nedåtrisk för vår prognos. På fredag publiceras tillväxtdata för augusti och starka sentimentsindikatorer talar för en tydlig rekyl uppåt, efter lite svaga siffror i juli. Momentum för tillväxten ser ut att ha förstärkts under tredje kvartalet, men höga energipriser och höjd ränta talar för att utsikterna framåt är inte lika ljusa. KPIF-inflationen kommer enligt vår bedömning stiga till 1,6% i september och kombinationen av höga världsmarknadspriser och reversering av skattesänkningar på drivmedel gör att inflationen ser ut att stiga till 2,5% under slutet av året. Det återstår att se hur de till sist lite mer optimistiska hushållen kommer reagera på en ny kostnadschock. Riksbankens räntehöjningar kommer att driva upp den totala KPI-inflationen till 2,5-3% under 2027 vilket talar för tydliga nedåtrisker för vår optimistiska BNP-prognos 2027.
SEB:s Boprisindikator, som publicerades nu på morgonen, stiger med 2 enheter till 43
. Indikatorn har varit ganska stabil under 2026 på relativt höga nivåer och vår prognos – att bostadspriserna stiger med 5% i år – ser ut att vara på spåret. Tidiga och större förväntade räntehöjningar från Riksbanken är en nedåtrisk för bostadspriserna under 2027. Mäklarstatstik presenterar bostadspriser för augusti på torsdag. Mer om vår indikator 
här.
Försöken att bilda en ny regering fortsätter, 
men förutsättningarna för en rödgrön regering ser än så länge osäkra ut. Centerpartiet har bjudit in S, V och MP till en gemensam lägesgenomgång på fredag, men håller samtidigt fast vid sin röda linje att inte sitta i samma regering som Vänsterpartiet. Centerpartiet Magdalena Andersson ska redovisa resultatet av sina sonderingar till talmannen senast den 12 oktober, men kan begära mer tid om meningsfulla samtal fortfarande pågår. Talmannen har sagt att en statsministeromröstning ska hållas när sonderingsuppdraget är avslutat. SvD
Stora Coop sänker priserna på 600 av sina mest sålda varor
 med i genomsnitt 6,5% i hela landet. Det är åtminstone ytterligare ett tecken på att konkurrenstrycket i dagligvaruhandeln är högt och ger inget stöd för någon bred ny prisuppgång på livsmedel just nu.

articles.title: Higher home price sentiment
articles.heading: SEB Housing Price Indicator (Sweden)
articles.fulltext:
The SEB Housing Price Indicator rebounded in October, rising by 2 units to 43. Housing market sentiment has been relatively stable so far this year and in October was largely in line with where it was in January. The most recent data suggests that overall consumer confidence has risen above the historical average, closing the spread vs the housing price indicator. The October Housing Price Indicator also reveals a view of rising interest rates triggering a higher share who are planning to fix mortgage rates.
Key points
Home price sentiment rose 
by 
2 index points to 43 in October, almost the same level as at the start of the year, as more respondents expect higher prices
Sentiment has stayed above its historical average for more than a year
Households’ interest rate expectations continue higher, and 15% 
plan
 to fix rates
The housing market sentiment has been relatively stable for a long time and has now remained above the 
historical
 average for more than a year. Hence, as indicated in various other economic sentiment indicators
,
 the strong headwinds from higher energy prices and geopolitics 
do
 not appear to have left a negative mark on economic activity.
Households’ home price 
sentiment has 
for some time been stronger than consumer confidence would imply.
 However, the last consumer confidence reading suggested Swedish households finally becoming more upbeat than the 
historical
 average for the first time since 2021. Consumption data also suggest
s
 stronger activity and the overall impression suggest
s
 a more solid footing for Swedish households. That being said, elevated energy prices are now also affecting all energy consumption and the most recent switch in the prospects for the policy rate add to these headwinds (read more 
here
).
The higher reading in the October indicator was driven by 
the 
share of respondents expecting prices to increase (from 51% in September
 to 53% in October)
,
 while the share expecting prices to decline was unchanged (
as was the share
 expecting prices to be unchanged)
.
In the October survey we see respondents preparing for higher policy rates, but there was also a relatively large change in the share planning to fix mortgage rates. However, since the beginning of July
,
 2y mortgage bond yields have already risen by 70bp, so it remains to be seen what 
those with
 a 3M mortgage rate will do (currently 80% of the stock).

articles.title: Unexpected employment slowdown supports Fed pause in October
articles.heading: US Economy
articles.fulltext:
Payroll employment (NFP) growth slowed to only 29k in September, well below all estimates ahead of the data, and with new large downward revisions to previous months. The unemployment rate increased, reflecting a reversal in the participation rate, and earnings growth slowed. Employment data is notoriously unreliable, but the modest performance according to the new data adds further support to some Fed members’ calls for an October pause. 
Key points
Nonfarm payrolls grew by 29k (estimated 90k, previous 133k, revised from 162k)
Downward revisions of 60k over the past two months
Unemployment rate increased to 4.2% (estimated unchanged at 4.1%)
Labour force participation rate increased to 61.8% (estimated unchanged at 61.6%)
Hourly earnings slowed to 0.1%, 3.0% y/y (estimated unchanged at 0.3%, 3.1%)
Slower employment growth goes against recent signs of accelerating activity but not necessarily a sign of weakness
Support for a Fed pause in October
Volatile data but not sending the same strong signals as before 
US labour market reports is one of the data with most market impact, and one of the hardest to predict, given a large monthly volatility and often substantial revisions. One should therefore be careful to draw conclusions from single months. An unusually low response rate in September is another reason for caution this time. Still, the large downward surprise in September means that we are again back in the “low-hire, low-fire” description of the labour market, with sluggish employment growth but also very low layoffs.
No reason for the Fed to worry about labour market weakness
The Fed has for some time described the labour market as stable and enabling it to focus on the too high inflation. Stricter immigration policies/deportations and an aging population means that the break-even employment growth needed for a stable labour market is lower than before. Thus, the slowdown in job creation in September should not necessarily be seen as a sign of weakness by the Fed. Fed staff in an analysis earlier this year concluded that even months with negative employment changes could become the new normal in this situation. The current 3-month average employment growth of around 50k should be in line with estimates for the new break-even of 30 to 60k per month. The small increase in the unemployment rate should also not be a sign of concern given the volatility in this data and a mostly downward trend this year.
Support for an October Fed pause 
Still, we believe the data should support the views among some influential members of the Fed, vice Chair John Williams and vice Chair Philip Jefferson, that the Fed could take time to evaluate the September hike. The fast employment growth seen in August added to the picture of continued resilient and perhaps even accelerating US growth and has by many in the Fed been seen as a sign that policy is not restrictive enough to bring inflation back to target. That conclusion is less obvious given the slowdown and downward revisions in the September report. 
September employment below all estimates, back to mostly downward revisions
The overall increase in non-farm payrolls at 29k was below the low range in the consensus estimates (35k to 180k) and well below the median estimate (90k). Downward revisions were 60k and we are again back in the pattern with mostly downward revisions.
Non-cyclical employment not the same driver now
Government jobs declined by 17k, after a temporary uptick in September. Private health care and social assistance continue to add jobs but at a slower pace than before (September +23k). Taken together, employment in non-cyclical sectors, which have at times been the key driver for the labour market, was little changed in September (+3k). Employment within cyclical sectors is showing a weakening trend too. Ongoing job losses within especially information (-10k) and financial activities (-7k) could be a sign that AI is affecting some sectors of the economy. The renewed decline in temporary health services (-11k) is a generally weak sign, since this is presumably the category of workers where firms would begin when needing to cut down its work force. Employment within leisure and entertainment has been volatile during summer, perhaps partly reflecting effects of the World Cup, and slowed again in September (+10k).
Higher unemployment rate should alleviate any concerns of overheating
The unemployment rate edged higher again, from 4.1% to 4.2%. This reflects a further recovery in the participation rate, which is normally a sign of strength for the labour market, though this time it follows a steady downward trend during this year. 4.2% is still well in line with the Fed’s view of a stable labour market and a single month’s change should not affect their views much. Still, the upturn should help alleviate any concerns that an increased demand for workers could eventually force companies to pay more to attract workers.
Low earnings growth means that the labour market is not currently an inflation risk 
Earnings growth slowed (0.2% m/m, 3.0% y/y, down from 0.3%/3.1%). Given productivity growth of 2% y/y or more, this should not be a threat to the inflation target. Hourly earnings data in the employment report is not adjusted for changes in the mix of workers and can also be affected by calendar effects depending on the dates in the survey week. We view wages according to the quarterly Employment Cost Index, ECI, as a more reliable measure, but the message from both sources is the same, that the labour market is not a source of inflation at present.
Dovish market reactions
The market reacted by further lowering the probability of an October rate hike to around 20% (5 bp) but continues to fully price a December hike (25 bp accumulated). The market is now pricing a total of three additional rate hikes in 2026 and 2027, after the September increase. We have predicted one more rate increase by the Fed in December, and a return to rate cuts again in late 2027 and see no reason to change these views because of this data.

articles.title: Busy global agenda with Fed and ECB minutes in focus
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
The coming week offers a busy global agenda, with central bank communication and key inflation data in focus. Fed and ECB minutes, together with several ECB speeches, will be closely watched following the recent rise in yields. In Sweden and Norway, September inflation will take centre stage, while the French and Norwegian budgets and EU-China trade talks add to the political agenda.  
US:
Fed minutes will be in focus following the unexpectedly hawkish Fed rate projections, the more hawkish shift in market expectations over the autumn, and the sharp upturn in yields. We will also get more input on service-sector activity from the ISM, following the recent very strong signals from the services PMI.
Euro area: 
Industrial production for major economies will be interesting. Also, German industrial orders can help shed some light on production in the near term. There will be lots of ECB speeches and the ECB will publish its account of Sept. 9-10 policy meeting. Finally, the formal submission of the French budget for 2027 (October 6) and the EU-China trade talks 8-9 October will be important.
Sweden:
September CPI is the main event. Growth indicators for August, service sector PMI, the budget balance, home prices from Mäklarstatistik and our own Housing Price indicator will be of interest this week as well. 
We also keep an eye on the Riksbank Governor Thedéen's speech on Thursday.
Norway:
The government’s budget proposal for 2027 due Wednesday will draw attention this week, and a number of budget measures have been leaked, suggesting increased spending on a broad range of social and defence related posts. Fiscal policy will likely remain somewhat expansionary though to lesser extent than in previous years. Friday’s inflation data for Sep will be of high importance for the market. Norges Bank lowered its near-term forecast by as much as 0.5ppt in its Sep MPR and we see upside risk to its near-term trajectory.

articles.title: An update of current market views
articles.heading: Macro Trading Strategy
articles.fulltext:
FX: Euro view challenged (stuck in a range before weak USD in 2027); short EURCHF overlay starting to play out; short SEK view since April shifted to only play it against JPY (prudent to scale back long EURSEK and NOKSEK)
We had argued a few weeks back in the 
FX Pilot
 that Euro is stuck in a range but probably to test the downside before breaking out higher in 2027
. Risks (France and gas prices) are ‘known knowns’ and should have less broad contagion risk. Clearly 
this story is challenged
 as Euro is breaking levels – we crudely estimated that around 1.10 in EURUSD the CTA type positioning should be max short.
O
ur view has been that playing a longer-term weak USD view in 2027 is best expressed via low delta EURUSD calls given the risks (updated charts below from September FX Pilot).
With that said we argued in September for running a short EURCHF overlay which is starting to play out.
French fiscal issues at risk of spilling over to Euro – should imply EURCHF lower as in 2024/25.
Positive news on Hormuz/oil – helps low yielders, goes against the carry trade (carry strategies are inherently long commodity beta), while positioning is very short CHF. 
Escalation of the oil/negative bond vortex – risks spilling over to equities as in March and imply EURCHF lower.
Meanwhile – SNB is de facto easing policy by allowing the real policy rate to drift into negative territory while the REER is depreciating – i.e. they could allow FX to do some of the tightening here.
On 
Monday
 this week we dialled back negativity on SEK vs European crosses (EUR and NOK) – but keep short SEKJPY.
SEK is very short positioned (like CHF) with the risk that French issues spill over to Euro while the gas price support for NOK should start stalling during October near peak EU ‘restocking’. I.e. it looked prudent to scale back SEK short views vs Euro and NOK as short covering could take hold.
With that said, sticking with a view of short SEKJPY (& CADJPY) – as a carry efficient way to play long Yen while having some ‘protection’ for a 2022 redux. Should a clear energy price disinflation impulse emerge look to only express long Yen vs CAD and USD. 
Interest Rates: Playing the Fixed Income bear market via ‘Macro RV’ implementations in NOK (AUD) and SEK:
I have certainly been directionally wrong, thinking we were priced for sticky inflation about 40bps ago …
Three thematic drivers have coincided with algo positioning getting to an extreme short position in longer bond futures - the themes being:
AI crowding out bonds both via equities attracting capital (foreign net purchases of US securities has entirely pivoted to equities from US treasuries) and corporate debt issuance.
Decent growth backdrop (AI capex driven) and a geopolitical inflation impulse.
Japan capital outflows stalling and possibly reversing.
Currently these themes and positioning (discussed above) are coinciding for a ‘peak bond crisis’ – question is where the narrative can change ahead?
The obvious one is that we get some progress on opening Hormuz – allowing for carbon molecules to flow freely but also importantly releasing shipping capacity/reducing transfer costs. This seems unlikely in the coming month ahead of US midterms.
Otherwise, the bond market needs the ‘automatic stabilizer’ to kick-in, i.e. equity markets to correct/a dent in the AI theme (or global PMIs to roll over). Markets are certainly trading as if the bond sell-off won’t stop until equities take a hit.
We have taken a very nitty gritty/defensive view of how to play the rates sell-off via positioning for front FRA-spread steepening in Norway (equivalent could have been done in Australia) 
– more in Norway 360 publications 
here
:
The high yielders (Norway and Australia) have had distinct curve shapes as they seem closer to a peak in the hiking cycle with very front FRA spreads having traded below/near zero (e.g. Dec26/March27). 
As long as these central banks can be seen as not cutting rates within 6 months these micro steepeners are essentially cheap optionality on hiking cycles having to be extended further. This has worked in Australia in particular but there should be more potential in Norway, looking for Dec26/March27 spread to get to 12bps (right chart below). 
In the coming weeks one will have to assess whether to extend micro steepening to March27/June27 if it trades below zero.
Norway and Australia are arguably running restrictive policy which should justify curve inversion into the belly. 
In Norway we opted (too early) for a view of June27/June28 inversion – this still looks like an interesting expression in both Norway and Australia though. 
Combined with the very front steepener view (discussed above) one essentially ends up with an implicit fly expression, e.g. pay belly of Dec26/June27/June28.
In Sweden we have opted to play long SGBs on ASW as a catch-up to the move higher in yields & a risk-off hedge while fading the pricing for Riksbank hikes on spread to Europe in 1Y1Y 
– more in Sweden 360 publications 
here
.
The SGB ASW trades directionally with yields but lagged the initial move higher in rates – 
i.e. there was a good case for a bid returning for bonds at attractive levels while also providing a ‘risk-off’ implementation.
 This trade has now blown past our take profit target.
Received 1Y1Y Stibor vs ESTR 
has had a correction lower again with the dislocation in European rate markets, making it interesting to replay the substantial Riksbank/ECB convergence priced.

articles.title: Elevated core inflation, but big test still ahead of us
articles.heading: Euro area inflation
articles.fulltext:
Both headline and core HICP remain elevated, but core inflation has moved broadly sideways for most of 2026. We continue to see little evidence of adverse spillovers from elevated energy prices, and the rise in core goods prices are attributed to other driving forces. The big test for projections when it comes to indirect effects due to high energy prices still lies ahead of us.
September HICP 3.8% y/y (SEB 3.5%, cons. 3.7%) and core HICP 2.5% y/y (SEB 2.4%, cons. 2.5%).
Key points
Broader energy prices key driver, little evidence of spillovers
The longer trend of higher core goods prices continues
Perhaps the first sign of rising food prices.
Elevated headline and core but still in line with the ECB staff projections
The October inflation report confirms the trends shown in previous national wide data releases. Headline HICP continues rising as high energy prices now have broadened from fuel to home energy prices like natural gas and electricity. As was the case in 2021/2022 contract structure and methodology differences will widen the spread from a cross-country perspective.
More importantly, core inflation remains elevated but in the past few months it has been more of a sideways movement, averaging around 2.4%. The October readings for both headline and core HICP are in line with the ECB Staff projections from September.
The 2026 core trend continues
While core inflation has moved roughly sideways in 2026 the underlying trend has been gradually higher 
for
 core goods prices while there has been a softening of the elevated service prices. While the latter is due to somewhat softer demand and wages, the former is partly explained by a trend of higher ICT and medicine prices, a trend which started already at the beginning of this year. 
We would also like to remind readers that service prices have been erratic over the past few years. Our impression is that this partly reflects changes in the seasonal pattern, and we have therefore preferred to assess the full set of August-November period before drawing any firm conclusions. The decline in September service prices this year was less than in the past few years but in the lower range taken by a longer historic metric. Hence, we await details to give more insight into this.
Test of spillovers still ahead of us
The key issue from a monetary policy perspective is any adverse spillovers from higher energy prices to a broader range of prices. These indirect effects normally happen with an extensive time lag. We and the ECB have the same profile for these indirect effects, and they start appearing by the end of this year and mostly during H1 2027. Hence, the test for how strong this effect will be is still ahead of us. Hence, up until October the narrative of little evidence of indirect effects remains.
Food prices are still on the soft side
During the September ECB Press conference, President Lagarde highlighted that the ECB had been surprised by developments in food prices. It is plausible that unprocessed food prices would respond more quickly to high energy prices and other supply-side disruptions. However, after several years of declining global food prices, the downward pressure on consumer prices appears to have been stronger—or it may still be a question of timing.
We continue to see relatively subdued food price developments, although we acknowledge the relatively large rise in unprocessed food prices in Italy. Indeed, the euro area as a whole recorded its first increase in overall food prices since April, driven by unprocessed food prices.
No policy implications
The October inflation figures are in line with the ECB staff projections, and we continue to see little evidence of significant spillovers. We therefore do not expect today’s figures alone to change the ECB’s assessment, and we continue to expect the next rate hike in December.

articles.title: October volatility as markets gauge prospects for Iran War escalation
articles.heading: Conflict Update
articles.fulltext:
Key points
Diplomacy between the US and Iran remains deadlocked. 
Crude oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz has recovered, but many other factors show normality is far from reached. 
An unstable equilibrium exists in which the Iranian regime will not accept peace without regime stability, whereas the US will not accept peace without regime compliance. 
US options for escalating military action remain limited only by our imagination and the Trump administration's track record for significant risk-taking and unpredictability. 
We believe renewed strikes are more likely to provoke large-scale Iranian retaliation against regional energy infrastructure and trigger a wider conflict rathern than to produce a deal, setting up October as a volatile month for markets. 
In last week’s 
note
, we argued that the stage appears set for an escalation in the conflict if parties failed to accelerate the path to negotiations. 
The diplomatic track between Iran and the US appears as intractable as ever.
 Last week’s proposal by Iran, which effectively sought a accelerated version of the MoU, was quickly rejected by Preisdent Trump. And, after no discernible progress was made during weekend meetings between Iranian officials and Qatari mediators, the disagreements between Iran and the US even extended to the manner of the Iranian delegation left New York. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordered “on Monday that Foreign Minister Araghchi and his delegation had to leave New York immediately” according to the 
Associated Press
. This was 
denied
 by the Iranian mission to the UN, which said that the departure had been planned well in advance. 
A war by many means.
 This week has seen an 
attempted disruption
 at a US-run air force base in the UK as well as a suspected terrorist attack on a flight between the UAE and Israel. Meanwhile, traffic through the Strait of Hormuz (SoH) shows it reaching roughly 
two-thirds
 of pre-war levels. This has raised questions about whether Iran has lost its 
leverage
 in the SoH. But as long as tanker insurance costs - as well as the risk of escalating kinetic attacks - remain elevated, this should not be interpreted as a return to normality. Front-month Brent futures continue to hover around 100 $/bbl, and this does not take into account tanker freight costs, which have soared this year, or the even higher prices of oil product such as diesel. 
The Iranian threat around the SoH remains persistent.
 Iranian attacks on commercial shipping in the SoH 
continue
, and there have also been 
reports
of injured US military personnel on a “maritime vessel”. Broader attacks on US Navy warships have not been independently verified, but open-source investigators have noted that the US blockade line appears to have 
shifted
 from the mouth of the Gulf of Oman to further out into the Indian Ocean, presumably to avoid Iranian anti-ship ballistic missiles. While this may not prevent the US from enforcing its blockade on Iranian shipping through the SoH transit, it does indicate a need to adjust to a more aggressive Iranian projection of military power in the region.
Recent events appear to have cemented the prevailing, and opposing, views of the US and Iran. 
The US, for the moment, appears satisfied with its current strategy under which they hope additional economic and military pressure will eventually force Iran to make significant concessions, if not capitulate outright. The Iranian regime has made clear such concessions will not be forthcoming. Instead, Iranian officials project the view that, by absorbing significant damage to Iran’s economy, the US will ultimately face growing economic and political incentives to compromise.
 This has led to an inherently unstable equilibrium in which the Iranian regime will not accept peace without regime stability, whereas the US will not accept peace without regime compliance.
A post-midterm escalation?
 Several Iran analysts have been warning of another round of fighting, before or after the midterms on November 3rd (see for example these two recent podcast episodes with 
Hamidreza Azizi
 and 
Trita Parsi
, respectively). The argument is that, freed from electoral constraints, especially if in the event of an electoral setback, the Trump administration could see stronger incentives to once more escalate the conflict in the hope of finding a lever with which to compel Iranian regime compliance.
‘Titanic Fury’ and other bad options.
 Reports of another possible round of escalation have fuelled speculation about possible targets, which could include renewed strikes on similar targets to those hit in March (military installations, deployed missile systems, and civilian infrastructure) or those struck in July (focusing more on military installations around the Strait of Hormuz). Another possibility is a strategic strike on nuclear targets like Pickaxe Mountain (which is reported to house some of Iran’s remaining nuclear capabilities), an attempt to use special forces to extract highly enriched uranium (HEU), or an attempt to seize the oil terminals at Kharg Island. The Trump administration could also seek to dust off previously discarded options of arming the opposition, in particular Kurdish militant groups operating out of northern Iraq. The normally unthinkable scenario where the US could seek to use a 
tactical nuclear weapon
 on an Iranian target needs to be seen in the light of a US presidential administration whose Middle East policies have been plagued by poor planning, an overreliance on military force, rash and unpredictable actions, and a disregard for the strategic consequences of its actions. The combination of Trump’s Nixonian ‘madman theory’ with the religiously and nationalistically infused ironclad resolve of the Iranian regime makes for a combustible mix in resolving conflict. 
October volatility ahead as markets gauge prospects for renewed escalation.
 A best-case scenario is that renewed US strikes become a catalyst for more fruitful negotiations, ultimately leading to a diplomatic solution. Yet a more likely outcome is that they fail to coerce an already hardened regime with existential fears and a perception of the US as profoundly deceitful and untrustworthy. Iran may in turn retaliate against regional energy infrastructure in a manner consistent with previous attacks or worse. Such a move would then likely result in large-scale damage to Iran’s own energy infrastructure, which could reduce the likelihood of Iran escalating first. Serious attempts at US-backed Kurdish interventions in Iranian territory could potentially lead to Iranian attempts to 
invade
 Bahrain and Kuwait. The conflict, already widened by the Houthi offensive in Yemen, could expand further to include Iran-aligned Iraqi Shia militant groups targeting either Iraqi Kurdistan or Syria. Even if the White House calculates that an energy crisis is an acceptable price to pay for Iranian regime compliance, the global economy will be left to suffer. This sets up October as a potentially volatile month, as markets gauge the prospects of renewed escalation.

articles.title: Revised lower to 2.0%
articles.heading: Norwegian unemployment
articles.fulltext:
The seasonal-adjusted registered jobless rate was stable at 2.0% in September, after a downward adjustment of the August numbers. Unemployment is thus running marginally below Norges Bank’s 2.1% estimate. However, data overall continue to point to a stable and healthy labour market, in line with Norges Bank’s reasoning in the Sep MPR.
Registered unemployment: 
The unadjusted jobless rate fell 0.1ppt to 2.0% in September. The seasonal-adjusted unemployment rate was stable at 2.0%, after a downward revision to the August numbers. The number of fully unemployed persons fell by 642, while people on employment schemes increased resulting in unemployment incl. employment schemes being stable at 2.6% (SA). In unadjusted terms, fully unemployed persons amounted to 59.4k, part-time unemployed 22.9k and people on employment schemes totalled 12.8k. The latter two corresponds to 0.8% and 0.4% of the labour force, respectively.
In September, unemployment was broadly stable across most occupational groups, with the largest increase in engineering and ICT. Unemployment in these fields has risen over the past year though from a low level, and NAV reports that part of the increase is due to the petroleum sector. Unemployment is highest in travel and transport (3.5%), and lowest among professionals (1.0%) and health and care workers (1.1%).
New registered job vacancies were 44.5k in September, which was 3% higher than a year ago. Vacancies were highest within health care followed by the retail sector and service occupations. New registered job vacancies tend to be volatile on a monthly basis, but overall, it points to still healthy labour demand with the long-term trend moving sideways.
Implications Norges Bank:
 In its Sep MPR, Norges Bank forecasted the registered jobless rate to remain steady at 2.1% for the remainder of the year, rising gradually from Q1 2027 to peak at 2.4% in mid-2028. Due to the revision of the August numbers, unemployment is running 0.1ppt below Norges Bank’s forecast. However, we do not expect this to be decisive for whether Norges Bank delivers another rate hike or not. The overall picture is that unemployment and new registered job vacancies are stable, which is in line with Norges Bank’s view from the Sep MPR.

articles.title: US payrolls, gloom ahead of Sunday's Brazil election
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
U.S. Treasury yields fell back slightly on Thursday after hitting new highs but the 10-year was at 5.34% earlier in the day. That in turn led to some breathing room for the stock market (S&P 500 +0.2%; Nasdaq unchanged) despite yesterday's higher oil price. Treasury yields have been pushed upwards due to concerns about high inflation, and the development of energy costs. A possible escalation in the conflict between Washington and Tehran will be crucial for whether the recovery for US government bonds can continue. The stock market in Asia is heading for its worst week since July and the stock market in Europe is heading towards its worst since April.
Nonfarm payrolls and European inflation in focus.
 Today's US employment report can provide clues about what will be required of the Fed's interest rate policy. The focus today will also be on euro area inflation for September. In addition, data on unemployment in Norway and Spain, Brazilian and South Korean inflation and Russian GDP will be released. Japan's core inflation in September came in at 3% year-on-year. This was significantly higher than analysts' expectations but may have been affected by an unusually long weekend period (the so-called "silver week") that temporarily drove up certain price categories.
Gloomy prospects in Brazil's elections
. On Sunday, Brazil will hold the first round of general elections, where opinion polls show a tight race between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Over the past half century, Brazil's economy has stagnated both compared to other countries in the region and global average growth. The incumbent left-wing president, Lula, will soon be 81 years old, the same age Joe Biden was when he withdrew his candidacy for re-election in 2024. Despite his commitment to democratic institutions and a healthy attitude to environmental issues, he has according to 
The Economist
 failed to stimulate growth and restrain public spending. Apart from a simplification of the sales tax, economic reforms have not materialized. His term ends with the highest government bond yield in 10 years. His opponent, the 45-year-old Bolsonaro, denies that humans are causing climate change, questions democratic institutions such as the electoral process, and suggests that he will not respect the election results if Lula wins. He has been under investigation for alleged links to violent criminals, which he denies. His main political goal is to pardon his father, who was sentenced to 27 years in prison in September 2025 for planning a coup – including a plan to assassinate Lula – after failing to be re-elected president in 2022. Neither candidate appears to offer policies that simultaneously guarantee both democratic rights and more sustainable economic development. 
The French government wants to reduce the budget deficit for 2027 by €43 billion
 through spending cuts and tax increases. 
The plan 
freezes some pension increases and limits pay increases for civil servants, and would mean an adjustment of the deficit from 5.4% of GDP this year to 5% next year. France's public debt is at its highest level since World War II.
Military build-up in the Middle East.
 The U.S. will send more troops, including a 
third aircraft carrier group
, to the Middle East, while President Trump warns that new attacks on Iran could be on the way after the congressional elections in November. In addition
, 
Axios
 reports 
 that the U.S. has sent more anti-aircraft missiles to the Gulf states, with one of the motives reportedly being to reassure countries that energy facilities will be protected if Trump orders new attacks.

here
) and a preview of Swedish September inflation (
here
).

The krona strengthened against the euro yesterday and the OMXS30 index fell by 1.3%.
Speaker Andreas Norlén has called a press conference today at 11.00 a.m. in connection with the formation of the government. The Riksbank's annual 
research conference
 is entering its second day.

articles.title: Amerikansk sysselsättning, dystert läge inför söndagens Brasilien-val
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Amerikanska marknadsräntor föll tillbaka något under torsdagen efter att ha nått nya toppnivåer men 10-åringen på 5,34% tidigare under dagen. Det ledde i sin tur till visst andrum för börsen (S&P 500 +0,2%; Nasdaq oförändrat) trots gårdagens högre oljepris. De amerikanska räntorna har tryckts uppåt pga. oro över den höga inflationen, och utvecklingen av energikostnaderna. En eventuell eskalering i konflikten mellan Washington och Teheran blir avgörande för om återhämtningen för amerikanska statsobligationer kan hålla i sig. Börsen i Asien går mot sin sämsta vecka sedan juli och börsen i Europa mot sin sämsta sedan april.
Amerikansk sysselsättning och europeisk inflation i fokus.
 Dagens amerikanska sysselsättningsrapport (”nonfarm payrolls”) kan ge ledtrådar om vad som kommer krävas av Feds räntepolitik. Fokus idag kommer också ligga på euroområdets inflation för september. Därutöver släpps data på arbetslöshet i Norge och Spanien, brasiliansk respektive sydkoreansk inflation samt rysk BNP. Japans kärninflation i september kom in på 3% i årstakt. Det var betydligt högre än analytikernas förväntningar men kan ha påverkats av en ovanligt lång helgperiod (den s.k. ”silverveckan”) som temporärt drivit upp vissa priskategorier.
Dystra valutsikter i Brasilien
. På söndag håller Brasilien första omgången i de allmänna valen, där det i opinionsundersökningar har varit dött lopp mellan sittande president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva och utmanaren Flávio Bolsonaro. Under det senaste halvseklet har Brasiliens ekonomi, i stället för att ta fart, stagnerat både jämfört med andra länder i regionen och den globala genomsnittliga tillväxten. Den sittande vänsterpresidenten, Lula, fyller snart 81 år, samma ålder som Joe Biden var när han drog tillbaka sin kandidatur för återval 2024. Trots sitt engagemang för demokratiska institutioner samt en sund inställning till miljöfrågor så har han enligt 
The Economist
 misslyckats med att stimulera tillväxten och hålla tillbaka de offentliga utgifterna. Bortsett från en förenkling av omsättningsskatten har ekonomiska reformer uteblivit. Hans mandatperiod avslutas med den högsta statsobligationsräntan på 10 år. Hans motståndare, den 45-årige Bolsonaro, förnekar att människan orsakar klimatförändringarna, ifrågasätter demokratiska institutioner som t.ex. valprocessen och antyder att han inte kommer att respektera valresultatet om Lula vinner. Han har varit föremål för utredning på grund av påstådda kopplingar till våldsamma brottslingar, vilket han förnekar. Hans främsta politiska mål är att benåda sin far, som i september 2025 dömdes till 27 års fängelse för att ha planerat en kupp – inklusive en plan att mörda Lula – efter att ha misslyckats med att bli omvald till president 2022. Ingen av kandidaterna ser ut att erbjuda en politik som samtidigt garanterar både demokratiska rättigheter och en mer hållbar ekonomisk utveckling. 
Frankrikes regering vill minska budgetunderskottet för 2027 med 43 miljarder euro
 genom utgiftsnedskärningar och skattehöjningar. 
Planen 
innebär att vissa pensionshöjningar fryses och att löneökningarna för statstjänstemän begränsas, och skulle innebära en justering av underskottet från 5,4% av BNP i år till 5% nästa år. Frankrikes statsskuld ligger på den högsta nivån sedan andra världskriget.
Militär uppladdning i Mellanöstern.
 USA kommer att skicka mer trupper inklusive en 
tredje hangarfartygsgrupp
 till Mellanöstern, samtidigt som president Trump varnar för att nya attacker mot Iran kan vara på väg efter kongressvalet i november. Dessutom rapporterar 
Axios
 att USA skickat fler luftvärnsmissiler till Gulfstaterna, där ett av motiven ska ha varit att försäkra länderna om att energianläggningar kommer att skyddas ifall Trump beordrar nya attacker.

articles.title: Higher for longer priced in
articles.heading: SEB FI & FX Strategy
articles.fulltext:
At a glance:
In market focus.
 Oil and the Middle East; Inflation data; Long-end yields; France.
Global macro and risk appetite. 
Global bond yields have risen sharply in recent weeks, with the 10Y Treasury yield at a two-decade high. Equities have so far proved resilient, while credit has been under pressure since September. Strategically, the most damaging transmission channel from rates to risk appetite is a rise in interest rates large enough to slow GDP growth sharply. Neither the level of bond yields nor rates volatility looks high enough yet to threaten a significant slowdown, but there are warning signals for a possible equity correction. Bond yields have been moving in sync with oil prices, and positioning is heavily skewed towards higher yields. A reopening of the Strait of Hormuz or weaker macro data could therefore trigger a move lower in yields. We think risk assets are unlikely to move higher until the uptrend in rates is broken.
US macro: Strong growth, inflation relief.
 The underlying inflation trend is looking better after the larger than expected downward effect from revised methods for core PCE. Annualized monthly change in line with the target over the past three months has eased the pressure for another near-term rate increase. However, strong growth – with upward revisions to total GDP, firm underlying demand in Q2 and strong spending in August – support that current policy is not restrictive and raises risks for companies passing through rising energy costs to consumers. AI build-out is seen by most of the Fed as a near-term upside risk to both growth and inflation. Rising real yields pose new downside risks for growth and especially through any adverse equity market reactions, given the importance of positive wealth effects for consumers. Markets are pricing less than a 40% probability for an October rate hike (9bp) and a full rate hike in December – which we see as reasonable – followed by two to three additional hikes in 2027 – which we see as excessive.
USD short rates: Waiting for new impetus. 
Terminal SOFR has risen by around 185bp, to 4.85%, since the Iran conflict began at the end of February, and the past week has shown tentative signs of stabilisation. We think policy rate expectations have risen enough for now and see scope for consolidation, with markets waiting for a trigger for the next move.
USD bonds: Higher for longer increasingly priced in.
 The 10Y Treasury yield is above 5.30% after a sharp sell off, driven mainly by higher policy rate expectations, not inflation expectations or term premium. Fed pricing and market positioning are stretched, but the sell off needs a catalyst to fade. Conflict de-escalation or weaker growth data may be the likely triggers, and a correction lower in long yields could be rapid once momentum turns.
France: Rising fiscal concern.
 PM Lecornu's government presented its 2027 draft budget on 1 October, ahead of formal submission on 6 October. Large savings needs and opposition discontent threaten the minority government, while fiscal worries and a lack of reforms are pushing French yields higher. Next year's presidential election adds uncertainty, with candidates at both political extremes gaining in the polls (read more 
here
).
EUR short rates: Policy rate pricing looks complete for now.
 Forwards discounting more than 80bp of additional hikes by next autumn, and we think it will be hard for markets to push pricing materially further at this point. At the same time, markets are likely to resist pricing fewer than 75bp of hikes without a decisive breakthrough that brings a substantial, sustained decline in energy prices.
EUR bonds: France in focus. 
With short positioning stretched and ECB and Fed pricing sufficiently aggressive to account for inflation prospects, we maintain our base case that the 10Y Bund yield will trade predominantly in a 3.40-3.60% range in the near term. The rapid widening of OAT vs. Bund spreads looks concerning and is increasingly spilling over to other markets, but it is unlikely to affect ECB actions materially just yet.
EURUSD: Market already short, but the downside risk is growing.
 The wider US–EUR 2Y differential has driven EURUSD lower, but that driver now looks close to exhausted: US policy pricing is stretched and positioning is skewed toward higher yields. The market is also already short EURUSD, which helps explain why spot has held up better than the backdrop suggests. The risk has shifted lower over the past week, though. French stress is spreading to Italy and Spain, and options are pricing more protection against a weaker euro. A sustained break below support would confirm that the euro-area premium is reaching FX and open 1.10–1.11. The upside risk is a positioning-driven squeeze.
Forecasts. 
Links to SEB’s official 
macro
, 
central bank
 and 
financial
 forecasts.
USD bonds: Higher for longer increasingly priced in
Two weeks ago, we expected the 10Y Treasury yield to consolidate in the 4.90-5.10% range. With the 10Y now trading above 5.30%, our view of consolidation proved premature. We see yields as stretched, but the sell off needs a catalyst to fade, most likely conflict de-escalation or weaker growth data.
Pricing of rate hikes through end-2027 has risen by around 185bp in the US and 125bp in the euro area versus levels prevailing just before the Iran conflict escalated at the end of February. As argued in the previous SEB FI & FX Strategy, policy rate expectations have reached a level where markets will likely struggle to push them much further without new triggers. Any further rise in yields would therefore more likely have to come from a higher term premium, which has so far remained contained. Conversely, with an already aggressive policy path priced in and positioning heavily skewed towards higher yields, better prospects for conflict de-escalation or disappointing growth data could trigger a rapid unwinding of part of the discounted hikes and a correction lower in long yields.
Cumulative rate hikes from inception of the Iran conflict to end-2027 discounted by futures: Fed and ECB
Policy rate expectations remain the key driver. 
The rise in the 10Y Treasury yield has continued to track policy rate expectations (illustrated by the 3Y forward on the 1M SOFR rate in the chart below), in line with our conclusion on the Bund yield in the previous report.
Policy rate expectations (SOFR) and 10Y Treasury yield
Long US rates have tracked oil prices closely since the start of the conflict until recently. Since mid-September, however, yields have kept rising, despite some pullback in oil. The deviation probably reflects higher-for-longer policy rate expectations, but we think developments that bring oil prices lower would help to ease pressure on bond markets.
Oil prices and 10Y Treasury yield
Inflation expectations remain anchored. 
Despite higher oil and other commodity prices, long-term inflation expectations are well anchored. Both 10Y and 5Y5Y CPI swaps trade at the levels seen in February. The 10Y real rate, however, has climbed from around 1.15% at the end of February to nearly 2.40% currently. A substantial repricing of the policy path (higher for longer) combined with stable inflation expectations suggests markets trust the Fed's commitment to its inflation target.
Inflation expectations (10Y CPI swap) and 10Y real rate (SOFR-CPI swap), %
Term premium up only modestly since the conflict began. 
The term premium has trended higher in recent years, as investors demand greater compensation for holding long-duration Treasuries amid uncertainty over inflation and the Fed's policy path, fiscal supply, long-term debt sustainability, and a marginal buyer base shifting towards more price-sensitive investors. The Fed's ACM model, the measure most widely followed by markets, has moved broadly sideways since mid-2025 and risen only modestly since the end of February. It supports the view that the rise in yields has been driven mainly by higher-for-longer policy rate expectations.
US: Term premium in 10Y tenor according to the ACM and Kim&Wright models
Structural term premium risks skewed higher. 
The term premium in Treasury yields is still relatively low in a long-term perspective, and we see risks skewed towards a structural increase in the coming years. Investors are likely to demand higher compensation for duration, particularly if the hedging qualities of Treasuries against shocks are seen weakening, for example on (geo)political or structural grounds.
US: Term premium in 10Y tenor, long-term perspective
Even with a structural rise in term premium, other factors will likely matter more for Treasury yields over the next 6-12 months, notably inflation and growth prospects, which in turn hinge on conflict resolution. With positioning stretched, a correction lower could be rapid once upside momentum fades. Historically, however, a sustained decline in long yields has emerged only near the end of hiking cycles.
EURUSD: Market already short, but downside risks are growing.
 The wider US–euro-area two-year differential has driven EURUSD lower, but further US policy repricing looks increasingly difficult to sustain. European fiscal stress is becoming the more important downside risk. French spreads have widened sharply, Italy and Spain have begun to follow, and options are pricing more expensive protection against a weaker euro. Short CTA positioning leaves room for a squeeze, but we need to give weight to the risk that fiscal stress broadens and puts further pressure on EURUSD. A sustained break below support, accompanied by broader European stress, would open the way towards 1.10–1.11.
The rate differential has driven EURUSD lower, but that driver looks increasingly mature.
 Since the Iran conflict escalated, the implied end-2027 US rate has risen by around 185bp, compared with roughly 125bp in the euro area. The larger US repricing has widened the two-year differential and weighed on EURUSD. As argued in the USD rates section, however, US policy pricing looks stretched and positioning is skewed towards higher yields. A further sell-off increasingly requires a fresh catalyst, while additional upward pressure on long yields may come from term premium rather than policy expectations.
The risks to the differential are therefore becoming more two-sided. We see the hawkish US repricing as excessive, while ECB expectations may remain sticky unless energy prices fall decisively. A correction driven by softer US data could narrow the differential and support EURUSD. That would weaken one source of downward pressure on the pair, but would not necessarily offset a growing European fiscal risk premium
Fiscal stress is broadening across the euro area, although markets are still differentiating.
 OAT–Bund widening has been accompanied by a sharp rise in French CDS and French equity underperformance. Italy has followed, and Spain has now widened too. France remains under the greatest pressure and Spain the least, suggesting that investors are still distinguishing between sovereign risks. Nevertheless, the widening beyond France raises the risk that fiscal concerns become a broader euro-area problem.
Part of the move has tracked the global rise in long-end yields, led by US Treasuries. Higher financing costs amplify fiscal vulnerabilities, and a turn lower in US yields could therefore ease some pressure. If French spreads fail to narrow alongside that relief, it would strengthen the case that domestic fiscal concerns are sustaining the repricing.
For EURUSD, the escalation test is whether peripheral widening exceeds what global yields and the usual relationships with France would explain, and whether European banks begin to underperform. Those developments would strengthen the case that sovereign stress is becoming an independent driver of euro weakness.
EURUSD’s resilience is increasingly vulnerable to broader fiscal stress.
 Spot has weakened, but has not shown the same degree of stress as French sovereign markets. Our CTA proxy already indicates short EURUSD positioning, which may dampen additional selling from trend-following investors and leaves the pair exposed to short covering. FX may also still be treating French spread widening partly as an extension of the global rates move.
We see a growing risk that this resilience is challenged. The French spread to Bunds is at its widest since the euro-area debt crisis. Although it remains below the 2012 peak and does not imply the same systemic risks, the scale and speed of the repricing warrant attention. Italy and Spain beginning to follow increases the risk that the pressure extends beyond France. Existing shorts may slow the adjustment, but do not provide a floor if the underlying outlook deteriorates.
Protection is building in both directions, but most of all against a weaker euro.
 Implied vol has risen across the curve, lifting the cost of hedging both a stronger and a weaker EUR, so the market is pricing larger moves either way. The put side has led, though. One-month 10-delta put vol has jumped from around 5.5 to 8, and in 1Y, put vol has risen to its highest level in a year while the premium over at-the-money has widened. The market is not just hedging a break in the range: it is starting to pay for a more persistent EUR downside, while keeping upside convexity on the table.
Energy: still a risk, but with room for optimism. 
With the injection season over and the threat of a US diesel export ban receding, near-term energy pressure on Europe may ease. Winter and next year's refill season remain tight, so the risk has not gone away, but it is less likely to be the trigger for EUR weakness.
The downside risk for EURUSD has grown over the past week.
 French stress has spread to Italy and Spain, spot is testing the bottom of its 2026 range, and options are pricing more protection against a weaker euro. But positioning remains stretched, so the upside has not gone away.
Scenarios:
Downside: French stress reaching FX.
 The main downside risk is euro-area fiscal stress spreading beyond France. Watch for spreads widening beyond the move in global yields, together with European banks underperforming. In a market this short positioned, and but a sustained break lower, breaking resistant levels, would open 1.10–1.11. Even if there have been some energy relief, a persistent winter premium would still reinforce a break.
Upside, short term: a positioning-driven squeeze.
 The most likely upside trigger is US yields peaking. As argued in the USD rates section, policy pricing looks stretched and positioning is skewed toward higher yields. With more hikes priced in the US than in the euro area, a correction would likely narrow the 2Y differential, and short positions in Treasuries and EURUSD could unwind together. A manageable outcome to the French budget votes on 20 October and 17 November, together with easing diesel stress, would remove two euro-area brakes. That could lift EURUSD back above 1.15. Because the rally would be driven by positioning rather than fundamentals, we would treat it as a correction, not a turn.
Upside, longer term: disinflation and conflict resolution.
 A sustained EUR recovery needs global disinflation that lets markets lower rate expectations, that would most likely follow from an end to the conflict that brings oil prices down. That is more likely a 2027 story than a Q4 one.

articles.title: Ahead of September CPI
articles.heading: Swedish inflation
articles.fulltext:
Slightly higher core inflation in September
CPIF ex energy
 is predicted to increase to 0.7% y/y in September (August 0.5% y/y, Riksbank forecast: 0.7% y/y). 
CPIF 
is seen increasing markedly to 1.6% y/y (August 0.7% y/y Riksbank: 1.5% y/y), from 0.7% y/y last month. Both electricity and fuel prices rose sharply in September.
CPIF ex energy
 corrected for lower VAT and higher subsidy for public transport is expected to edge higher to 1.6% y/y in September (August 1.5% y/y, Riksbank forecast 1.8% y/y).
Gradually rising inflation from modest levels 
September is the first monthly reading after the September Monetary Policy report (MPR). The forecast for CPIF ex energy was largely unchanged compared to the June MPR. We predict core inflation to trend gradually higher over the next 6 months driven by a weaker SEK and expect some indirect effects from higher energy prices. The forecast for CPIF ex energy has been revised slightly higher due to upward revisions to the forecasts for rents in apartments and co-ops. Earlier and larger rate hikes from the Riksbank will exert upward pressure on rents. 
So far, near-term indicators, such as pricing plans and producer prices on consumer goods, have remained low; this is the case both in Sweden and in the euro area. Prices on package holidays, car rentals and hotels increased more than normal during the summer and price levels continue to be elevated, despite falling back in August. A continued normalisation is a downside risk to CPIF ex energy in September. 
Sharply higher energy prices in September. 
Fuel prices are set to rise by 14% and electricity prices by 9% m/m in September, driven by higher market prices. A reversal of temporary tax reductions on fuels means that energy prices will continue to rise sharply in Q4. Futures pricing indicate large price drops on both electricity and fuels over the next 6-12 months, but the decline has been delayed. Headline CPIF will rise well above the target in the beginning of next year, although the inflation rate will be very volatile. 
Policy implications
The Riksbank was more hawkish than expected in September and the meeting minutes confirmed that the probability for a rate hike in November is very high. None of the Board members discussed the possibility of hiking in both November and December, but this is the main scenario implied by current market pricing. We stick to our forecast for rate hikes in November, February and May and some recent retracing of aggressive market-implied expectations for near-term rate hikes from the ECB and the Fed supports our forecast. After the notable shift in policy stance in September, uncertainty has increased. Actual inflation, developments in the Middle East, as well as foreign central banks will decide the size and the timing of rate hikes.

articles.title: Long rates continue higher – despite oil below USD 100
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
US long rates continued higher yesterday.
 The 10-year yield is now very close to breaking above its highest level since the financial crisis, a milestone the 30-year yield already passed on Tuesday. The rise came despite inflation, as measured by the Fed’s preferred gauge, PCE, coming in below expectations and the market subsequently pricing a slightly lower probability of a rate hike in October. Long rates instead took greater cue from growth data that reinforced the picture of surprisingly resilient US growth in the first half of the year.
Equity markets were somewhat mixed, with tech-heavy Nasdaq edging higher while the S&P 500 declined. In Europe, country-level inflation data suggest that the 2.5% core inflation forecast may hold, although there is some risk of an upside surprise. Attention therefore shifts to growth, with PMIs for many countries and the US ISM on today’s agenda.
In Asia, equity markets that are open are generally higher, but note that Chinese markets are closed today and will remain closed until next Thursday owing to the National Day holiday. Equity futures point to a lower open in Europe but a higher open in the US.
Oil prices fell sharply overnight to USD 97 per barrel, without yet generating major headlines. According to 
Bloomberg
, attention has shifted towards oil flows out of the Middle East approaching pre-war levels, although it remains unclear whether quarterly effects may also be affecting the price.
Will the US ISM manufacturing index confirm last week’s strong PMI?
 Last week’s surprise rise in September PMI readings, to their highest levels in several years, was interpreted as further evidence of the surprisingly strong resilience of the US economy. However, we do not expect today’s ISM manufacturing index, released at 16:00 CET, to show a similar increase. Instead, the index is expected to be broadly unchanged, albeit at still solid levels. A decline in several regional manufacturing surveys in September also poses a downside risk. Beyond the headline figure, the ISM will be closely scrutinised for signs of renewed bottlenecks in prices and delivery times, in line with signals from both the PMI and several regional indices.
September and Q3 market wrap.
 With both September and the third quarter now behind us, both periods were characterised by higher oil prices and rates, a stronger dollar and a weaker krona. US equities, however, rose over the third quarter, even though they declined in September (see table below). One possible explanation is that the bulk of the move in rates did not occur until September, which also pushed yields to levels that are more challenging for equities.
In FX (charts below), high-yielding currencies outperformed in the third quarter while low-yielding currencies underperformed – a clear sign that carry trades dominated. One exception was the low-yielding JPY, which was supported by repeated interventions.
Nordic key stories
Riksbank minutes confirm the hawkish shift.
 The minutes confirm the hawkish shift from last week’s rate decision, but also show that views on the balance of risks still differ within the Executive Board. A rate hike in November looks highly likely, with further hikes expected next year. However, board members remain vague on the pace and extent of additional increases. The global outlook will be crucial, and energy prices remain an important factor for the rate outlook. We still expect rate hikes in November, February and May. Read more 
here
.
Recovery in Swedish manufacturing PMI.
 The September PMI is released at 08:30 CET, and we expect the index to show a recovery. This would see the PMI continue to reverse part of July’s unexpected decline, when the index fell after an upward trend since 2023.
